page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU features hyper-threading with 2 threads per core, 33 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. The instance provides 16.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It includes no bundled local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, features no GPU accelerators, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements place the compute and memory subsystem performance in lower tiers compared to newer cloud hardware. Single-core and multi-core evaluations under stress-ng register weak results (1102.59 and 2912.92 respectively), mirrored by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1989.0 and single-core score of 914.0. Memory throughput benchmarks show uncached read operations at 19.5 GB/sec and uncached write operations at 18.08 GB/sec. Workload-specific scores, including Clang compilation (2907.0), Redis SET throughput (2.96 million operations/sec), and PassMark database operations (1065.78), further highlight modest processing throughput across common application routines.

Given the balanced allocation of 4 vCPUs and 16 GB RAM alongside older Skylake-generation architecture, this instance offers moderate compute density suited for cost-sensitive environments rather than low-latency or compute-heavy processing. The absence of local NVMe storage and the 2 Gbps network baseline make it best suited for light-to-moderate general purpose workloads, secondary application tiers, small internal web services, development environments, and low-traffic background task processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.xlarge is a general-purpose KVM-based instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, while lacking bundled local storage and GPU acceleration. Network baseline connectivity is rated at 2 Gbps without included public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark assessments across stress-ng, Geekbench (914.0 single-core, 1989.0 multi-core), and PassMark place its compute and memory capabilities in the lower tiers of cloud hardware. It achieved 2.96 million operations/sec in Redis SET tests and 2.32 GB/sec in static web serving. The instance presents a cost-effective, balanced profile appropriate for moderate general-purpose tasks, small application backends, internal development servers, and low-throughput background services.
